account: So far today I have not established that anything unusual is happening. During my scheduled market walk, three townsfolk independently repeated that the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery. My neighbour also says the baker is making fresh bread for today's market. That fits ordinary bakery business; the repetition catches my attention, but it is not evidence of a secret undertaking. My neighbour says the riverside quarter is quiet and has confirmed our usual tea at three at the east-bank dockside cottage. The secretary has been confirming that address and my arrangements. Earlier she said the appointments chest was empty after I had returned the book; I subsequently saw her take a written book from that chest. She now assures me both days' appointments are safely back there. This may simply reflect her handling the schedule, not wrongdoing. She reports no correspondence or unusual business. Just now I saw freight near the book stall holding an emerald and the builder approaching from the bridge holding a lantern. I do not know their purposes; shopping and ordinary work are plausible. I should keep my noon lunch and one o'clock accounts appointment, attend tea at three, and listen for more concrete news rather than assume these ordinary activities are connected.
